name: FallenSoldier
source:
He clutched at his stomach as he fell. 
 
 Blood slowly pooled around him - nearby, his allies and comrades returned fire desperately. They'd likely survive if they could hold out long enough for reinforcements, but he knew he was done for. 
 
 The world went black. 
 
 -- - 
 
 He awoke to the taste of dirt in his mouth. Had he - 
 
 Next to him, his squadmates drew their weapons and returned fire. 
 
 -- - 
 
 Dirt. Blood. Gunfire. Ragged coughs. 
 
 The medic did n't make it in time. 
 
 -- - 
 
 How many times had it been? He'd long since forgotten. He filled his lungs, turned around, and yelled. 
 
 `` Hey, get do-'' 
 
 -- - 
 
 There was n't time to react. There never was. 
 
 He was becoming rather well acquainted with the ground. 
 
 -- - 
 
 It was pointless to try to do anything, so he went limp. 
 
 The bullet, as it always had, cut a burning line through his body. 
 
 Right through the belly button.
retelling:
From the perspective of **The Medic**, a battlefield medic tasked with saving lives amidst chaos:

The cacophony of gunfire and explosions permeated the open battlefield, each echoing pulse a stark reminder of the lives hanging by threads around me. Amidst the carnage, I could hardly miss the unmistakable trail of blood that stained the ground, leading to a fallen comrade who clung desperately to life.

His name was never spoken aloud, but I had learned his face well. The medic who had been with us since our first deployment together. His eyes were filled with fear and determination as he lay there, breathing weakly, blood pooling beneath him. Despite my best efforts to stanch the flow, it seemed an endless torrent, and I knew that he wouldn't make it.

Time stretched on, as I continued my frantic attempts to save him. The chaos of battle swirled around me like a storm, drowning out any semblance of order or sense. Yet in the midst of this tempest, there was an undeniable stillness - a quiet acceptance that even my best efforts could not break. His eyes met mine one last time, and I felt the weight of unspoken words hanging between us.

He closed his eyes, and with his final breath, the world seemed to shift around me. The deafening roar of battle faded, replaced by an eerie silence that sent shivers down my spine. My gaze was drawn back to the fallen soldier who lay before me, lifeless but still bleeding. I knew then, as surely as if I had seen it with my own eyes, that this cycle would continue indefinitely for him - a ceaseless loop of death and rebirth on the battlefield.

I stood there, frozen, unable to move or speak as I watched his body convulse one final time before dissolving into nothingness. The silence was shattered by the renewed cacophony of gunfire and explosions, and I knew that my duty remained unfinished. I would continue to fight alongside these brave men and women, offering hope where there seemed none, but always knowing that some sacrifices could not be undone.
